### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Hello,

This is my first issue repport with mini / my english is not perfect, sorry in advance.

I'm trying to have a file template for new php files.

To do so, I've made this autocmd : 
```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufNewFile", {
  pattern = "*.php",
  callback = function(args)
    local line_count = vim.fn.line("$")
    local first_line_content = vim.fn.getline(1)
    local file_has_content = line_count ~= 1 or first_line_content ~= ""

    if file_has_content == false then
      local lines = {
        "<?php",
        "",
        "declare(strict_types = 1);",
        "",
      }
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(args.buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { #lines, 0 })
    end
  end,
})
```

But, with mini.files it doesn't work.

If I do it with `:edit test.php`, it works.

I am aware of `MiniFilesActionCreate` event, but does my implementation really needs to be specific for mini.files ? Is there a reason why `BufNewFile` isn't triggered ?

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()
    require('mini.files').setup()

    -- Setup the autocmd
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufNewFile", {
      pattern = "*",
      callback = function(args)
        local line_count = vim.fn.line("$")
        local first_line_content = vim.fn.getline(1)
        local file_has_content = line_count ~= 1 or first_line_content ~= ""
        if file_has_content == false then
          local lines = {
              "This is a new file"
          }
          vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(args.buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { #lines, 0 })
        end
      end,
     })
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Open mini.files (using `:lua MiniFiles.open()`) and create a new file, synchronize (using `=` key), then open the buffer of this new file
> The new buffer will have no content

5. Create a new file using the edit command `edit my_new_file.txt`
> The new buffer will have "This is a new file" content.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

The BufNewFile event is triggered when starting to edit a file that doesn't exist.

As you observed, the event is triggered when using the `:edit` command.
One can also use the '%' character in 'netrw'(`:h netrw-%`).

This behavior is a bit too much for mini.files.

> I am aware of MiniFilesActionCreate event, but does my implementation really needs to be specific for mini.files ? Is there a reason why BufNewFile isn't triggered ?

The BufNewFile event is not triggered by mini.files during synchronization because the file is directly [created](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/7e55c3d2c04da134085a31156196836f80a89982/lua/mini/files.lua#L2740) on disk, without creating buffers. The synchronization is a batch operation, potentially handling multiple changes.
Thus, when the user opens the newly created file from mini.files, that file already exists.

You could adapt the following code snippet using the MiniFilesActionCreate event:

```lua
local add_skeleton_lines_to_new_file = function(path)
  if path:sub(-1) == "/" then return end -- directory
  vim.fn.writefile({ "This is a new file" }, path)
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "MiniFilesActionCreate",
  callback = function(args) add_skeleton_lines_to_new_file(args.data.to) end,
})
```

If you want the BufNewFile event to be handled in the same way, add the following:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufNewFile", {
  pattern = "*",
  callback = function(args)
    add_skeleton_lines_to_new_file(args.match)
    vim.cmd("edit!")
  end,
})
```

I think the issue can be closed as 'works as expected'.

Thank you for the detailed solution and the implementation !

I now understand why.

Have a nice day !

title: [mini.files] File creation doesn't trigger "BufNewFile" autocmd
